audit_findings.title: Perpetual growth may ignore the CABOMETYX patent cliff
audit_findings.mechanism: CABOMETYX erosion would reduce projected OE and invalidate the smooth growth and terminal-value assumptions unless replacement products offset it.
audit_findings.evidence: This composition of matter patent, with patent term extension, will expire in August 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The August 2026 composition-patent expiration is not itself a demonstrated revenue cliff because other patents and litigation currently may restrict generic entry through 2030 or later. Nevertheless, generic challenges are active, CABOMETYX generated $1,123.421 million of the $1,128.002 million of first-half 2026 product revenue, and terminal value supplies 46.3%-51.5% of operating value. A material erosion scenario absent from the smooth projections is therefore reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Model product-level CABOMETYX revenue and margin erosion under each live litigation outcome and generic-entry date, probability-weight zanzalintinib and other replacements, and rerun all scenarios and terminal values.

audit_findings.title: The equity bridge may omit non-current marketable securities
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash and current marketable securities but omits a separately reported non-current marketable-securities asset.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had $1.66 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, as compared to $1.75 billion as of December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error: $281.448 million of cash plus $557.937 million of current marketable securities exactly equals the $839.385 million bridge balance, leaving out $544.930 million of non-current marketable securities. Adding the entire omitted amount would raise bear, base, and bull values to approximately $34.25, $43.55, and $50.46 per share, respectively. All remain below the $59.01 market price, while the base buy-below level would rise only from $29.06 to about $30.48 after the 30% margin of safety. It therefore does not change the stated conclusion, although the bridge must be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Add the June 2026 non-current marketable securities, determine any operating-cash exclusion, and rerun the bridge and per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Large contingent licensing claims are not visibly represented
audit_findings.mechanism: Success-dependent milestones, option payments, and royalties reduce the pipeline OE implicitly credited through growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, in conjunction with these collaborative in-licensing arrangements and asset purchase agreements, we are subject to potential future development milestone payments of up to $ 441.5 million, regulatory milestone payments of up to $ 278.0 million, and commercial milestone payments of up to $ 2.5 billion, each in the aggregate per product or target, as well as royalties on future net sales of products.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates contractual maxima of up to $441.5 million of development milestones, $278.0 million of regulatory milestones, and $2.5 billion of commercial milestones per product or target, plus royalties. Those maxima are not present liabilities or expected payments, so they cannot be mechanically deducted. The record does not show whether the growth scenarios probability-weight these costs alongside pipeline success, leaving a potentially important but unquantified overstatement.
audit_findings.action: Map each projected pipeline asset to its contractual milestones, option fees, royalties, timing, and probability of success, then rerun OE using net probability-weighted cash flows.

audit_findings.title: Latest-year OE may reflect a trough in recurring R&D
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher recurring clinical-development spending would reduce normalized OE and the operating-value anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: We project our research and development expenses may increase for fiscal year 2026, as compared to 2025, primarily driven by increases in clinical trial costs, including the current and planned trials evaluating zanzalintinib, XB628, XB371 and XB010, and personnel expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing does not demonstrate that the 2026 anchor preserves the 2025 R&D decline: first-half 2026 R&D was $411.903 million versus $412.589 million in the comparable period, although second-quarter expense increased and management expects spending to rise during the remainder of 2026. The expected increase is forward-looking and unquantified, so it should be monitored rather than treated as a presently demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Replace the annualized interim R&D assumption with the eventual full-year 2026 run rate or management's quantified program budget, then rerun normalized OE without crediting pipeline growth separately from its required spending.

audit_findings.title: The anchor tax rate is below management's forward range
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $7.1-$28.3 million of annualized OE, or roughly $0.37-$1.48 per share in the base case
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher normalized effective tax rate reduces after-tax anchor OE and all discounted operating cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: We project that our effective tax rate may be between 21% and 23% in fiscal year 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The 16.9% rate cited by the finding applies to 2025, whereas the 2026 anchor is labeled latest actual and the first-half 2026 filed rate was 20.3%. Applying 21%-23% to first-half pretax income instead would increase tax by approximately $3.5-$14.1 million for the half year, or $7.1-$28.3 million annualized. Scaling the base operating value by that anchor reduction lowers base value by only about $0.37-$1.48 per share and cannot close the $17.49 gap between the $41.52 base value and $59.01 price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the anchor calculation uses the 2026 interim tax provision, then rerun the anchor at both 21% and 23% and separately document durable FDII and credit benefits.

audit_findings.title: Unresolved 340B proceedings may create an unbridged claim
audit_findings.mechanism: An unrecorded settlement, repayment, penalty, or operating restriction would reduce OE or require an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: At this time, it remains unclear what, if any, liabilities we might incur as a party to this ADR proceeding.
audit_findings.explanation: The ADR and state proceedings are existing claims, but the filing says the resulting liability remains unclear and provides no estimable loss range. No supplied evidence demonstrates an accrued or omitted amount, while an adverse ruling could also change future 340B discounts and operating cash flows. The record therefore cannot establish materiality or quantify the valuation effect.
audit_findings.action: Review the latest contingency accruals, ADR record, state notices, disputed transaction volumes, and counsel's probability assessment; estimate repayment, penalty, and prospective discount exposure and rerun OE and the bridge if supportable.
